changes.new:
Dominici's thesis studies end-to-end unlearning through data preparation
pipelines and feature stores \citep{dominici}. The author's research description
emphasizes provenance tracking and deletion propagation. This is directly
relevant to the whole-pipeline target in Equation~\eqref{eq:target}.
Our analysis fixes one ordered suppression operator and its feature graph,
then requires exact ridge-head and continuing-state recovery under a cumulative
deletion budget. These assumptions delimit our result; they do not exclude
corresponding guarantees from the thesis. Its operator semantics, retained-data
access, and evaluation could not be checked without the full text.
Our Boolean expansion is a specialization.

changes.old:
Recent work on predictive versus counterfactual auditing state also
overlaps with the broad memory-separation principle \citep{counterfactual}.
Its public code was inspected in the earlier literature audit, but its
full-paper proof and approximate-success semantics could not be checked.
We therefore make no theorem-level superiority or quantitative comparison
with that work. We claim the stated fixed-scorer, shared-feature ridge
construction, not a new general separation between prediction and
counterfactual information.
changes.new:
Tadakamalla et~al. study predictive versus counterfactual auditing state
\citep{counterfactual}. Their released threshold-family code uses a binary
history of length $t$: predictive queries test its total count, while
counterfactual queries test every threshold after flipping one event
\citep{counterfactualcode}. The former distinguish $t+1$ counts; the latter
jointly recover all $t$ history bits for $t\ge3$. Thus task-dependent
information requirements and exact reconstruction already have a concrete
antecedent. Our hard queries instead delete public blockers and return ridge
heads on the same stored features used for curation. Our sequential contract
also specifies fresh-state equality at the remaining budget. This compares
our contract with the inspected code, not the full scope of their paper.
The advertised approximate bound cannot be compared numerically with our
expected squared head-error bound until its success event and quantifiers
are available. We claim the stated fixed-scorer, shared-feature ridge
construction, not a new general prediction--counterfactual separation.

We acknowledge their related scope and make no technical comparison that

changes.new:
The
counterfactual-auditing comparison uses the pinned author implementation
\citep{counterfactualcode}: its query family and exact decoder were inspected,
but the full-paper proof and approximate-success quantifiers remain
unverified. For Dominici's thesis \citep{dominici}, the author and laboratory
pages establish its pipeline-unlearning scope; they do not establish its
operator-level guarantees or experimental results. Neither full text was
obtained. These are comparisons at the stated evidence levels, not complete
paper-to-paper comparisons or evidence that either work lacks our result.
